newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline tracks NYMEX higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline tracks NYMEX higher.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline prices surged higher late Wednesday, fueled by a run-up in gasoline futures, traders said.
"The Merc went bananas," one trader said of heating oil and gasoline futures, which reversed early losses to end the day modestly higher.

Unleaded basis in Chicago and Group Three was largely unchanged late in the day after rising steadily this week on talk of refiner buying and reports of a heavy Gulf Coast turnaround schedule, traders said.
Chicago unleaded remained 0.50/0.75 cents a gallon over NYMEX February unleaded for January deliveries, with premium 1.25 cent a gallon higher.
Group Three unleaded was talked 3.0/2.75 cents a gallon under the print.

Chicago low sulphur diesel for January deliveries firmed to 6.0/5.75 cents a gallon under NYMEX February heating oil, drawing some strength from continued talk of an outage at Amoco's 410,000 barrel per day Whiting, Ind., refinery.
Traders said Amoco trimmed output from a 120,000 barrel per day fluid catalytic cracker to 80,000 barrels per day. A refinery spokeswoman, citing company policy, declined comment.
High sulphur diesel was bid 7.0 cents a gallon under the print in Chicago and eased to 8.25 cents under in Group Three.
